description.narrative: (Uganda): With FY 2022 Malaria, MCH, FP and Nutrition funds, UHSS will: 1) improve leadership and accountability for health sector results; 2) increase availability and improve management of health system resources; and 3) strengthen community systems for quality health services. The focus will shift to addressing HSS barriers to improving Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health/Malaria and HIV activities..UHSS will support the Ministry of Health (MOH) to integrate the National Community Engagement and Social Protection strategy into broader health policy. UHSS will collaborate with service delivery partners to finalize the Community Health Extension Worker Pilot. UHSS will work with the MOH to improve data visibility at community service delivery points.UHSS will support human resources for health (HRH) and their MOH advisors will address gaps in public financial management, and monitor the use of external project funds. UHSS will work with local government facilities to improve financial planning and funding for primary health care. UHSS will support the MOH and regional referral hospitals to improve skills in telementoring, and support supervision. It will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address its impact; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; 4) improve access and utilization of micronutrients; and 5) improve access and utilization of vitamin A.Specific activities to reduce climate risks to health will include providing budget advocacy support to the MOH to plan for contingency resources for procurement of additional essential health commodities that may be required due to seasonal outbreak of diseases like diarrhea and pneumonia. UHSS will support priority districts to include contingency plans in their annual work plans to reduce climate risks to health....
